title: Mathematical Foundations, Spatial Fields & Noise Architecture

blocks.content: Engineering notebook from `docs/MATHEMATICAL_FOUNDATIONS_FIELDS_AND_NOISE.md`. This archive preserves the project’s original rationale, equations, performance reports and illustrative code. Historical paths, API names, claims and sketches can differ from the current engine. For copy-ready programs use the guides and demos; for current callable signatures use the source-derived API. Performance figures here describe reported experiments, not guaranteed frame rates.

blocks.text: Original document: [docs/MATHEMATICAL_FOUNDATIONS_FIELDS_AND_NOISE.md](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/docs/MATHEMATICAL_FOUNDATIONS_FIELDS_AND_NOISE.md). See [current limitations](/limitations) for concrete compatibility notes.
Retiam is engineered from the ground up for rigorous mathematical animations, scientific simulations, and procedural graphics. Its mathematical architecture spans four major components:

To recreate the iconic mathematical animations pioneered by 3Blue1Brown—where arbitrary drawn shapes or SVG paths are traced by a chain of rotating epicycle circles—Retiam implements a high-performance DFT engine.
Given a sequence of $N$ complex numbers $z_k = x_k + i y_k$ sampled along any closed or open 2D path, the Discrete Fourier Transform evaluates the complex coefficients $c_n$:

blocks.tex: c_n = \frac{1}{N} \sum_{k=0}^{N-1} z_k \cdot e^{-i \frac{2\pi n k}{N}} \quad \text{for } n \in \left[-\frac{N}{2}, \frac{N}{2}\right]

blocks.text: The continuous parametric curve $Z(t)$ is reconstructed at phase $t \in [0, 1]$ via the Fourier series:

blocks.tex: Z(t) = c_0 + \sum_{n \neq 0} c_n \cdot e^{i 2\pi n t}

items: **`magnitude` (Default)**: Sorts harmonic coefficients in descending order of their radius $|c_n|$. The largest dominant circles rotate at the base of the chain, while high-frequency micro-variations refine the tip.
**`frequency`**: Orders harmonics by alternating frequencies ($0, +1, -1, +2, -2, \dots$).
**`none`**: Retains standard DFT array layout.

blocks.text: Vector fields in Retiam are represented by the [`ISpatialField`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/math/fields/SpatialField.ts#L15-L40) interface, mapping $\mathbb{R}^3 \times [0, 1] \to \mathbb{R}^3$:

items: **Zero-Allocation Buffer Evaluation**: For high-performance particle swarms and dense vector grids, `evaluateBuffer` mutates continuous `Float32Array` buffers directly without allocating intermediate objects:
**Piping & Composition**: Fields can be chained sequentially:
**Temporal Blending**: Linearly interpolates two vector fields over time factor $\alpha$:
**Spatial Falloff Masks**: Localizes field influences within a spherical radius using `smoothstep`, `linear`, or `gaussian` decay:

**Conformal Mappings**: Maps complex functions $f(z)$ while strictly preserving angles (Cauchy-Riemann equations $\frac{\partial u}{\partial x} = \frac{\partial v}{\partial y}$ and $\frac{\partial u}{\partial y} = -\frac{\partial v}{\partial x}$).
**Vortex / Swirl Fields**: Rotates space around a singularity with angular velocity proportional to $1 / r^k$.
**Source / Sink Fields**: Divergent or convergent radial vector flow fields.
**Electric Dipole Fields**: Exact electrostatic field generated by positive and negative point charges.
**`PerlinNoise`**: Classic Improved Perlin gradient noise with quintic Hermite smoothing ($6t^5 - 15t^4 + 10t^3$) avoiding lattice directional artifacts.
**`SimplexNoise`**: Higher dimensional simplex lattice noise ($O(N^2)$ evaluation complexity vs $O(2^N)$ for Perlin).

items.text: **`WorleyNoise` (Cellular Noise)**: Computes distances to pseudo-random Poisson feature points:
children: $F_1$: Distance to nearest cell point (Voronoi cell interior).
$F_2 - F_1$: Cell boundaries (stone textures, biological membranes, water caustics).

items: **`ValueNoise`**: Cubic interpolated lattice value noise.
**`WhiteNoise`**: Fast pseudo-random white noise.

blocks.text: All noise generators implement multi-octave fractal synthesis:

items: **Domain Warping**: Feeding one noise function into another to generate fluid-like marble, atmospheric clouds, and turbulent smoke:
**`Brace`**: Manim-style curly bracket attached to entities or coordinate ranges. Automatically calculates curved Bézier tips and provides a dedicated anchor point for LaTeX text labels.
**`Arrow` & `Arrow3D`**: Vectors with automatic scale-independent heads that maintain optimal visual proportions regardless of arrow shaft thickness.
**`PixelGrid`**: Displays 2D numeric matrices or convolution filters as discrete, animated pixel grids with value labels, borders, and heatmaps.
**`BooleanOps`**: Evaluates 2D constructive polygon operations (Union, Difference, Intersection, XOR) on arbitrary polygonal paths.
